item.title: A Message to All Staff: Everbridge Emergency Notification System Test
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Everbridge Emergency Notification System Test

Dear CRPD Team,

Yesterday afternoon we conducted a test of the Everbridge emergency notification system. Everbridge is our essential communication tool for notifying you in the event we need to close facilities or adjust activities to ensure the safety of the community, our staff and our facilities during inclement weather or other emergency. 

Yesterday, around 3:50 p.m., you should have received an email, phone call and/or text message based on the contact information you’ve provided in Dayforce. If you have not yet done so, please confirm that you received it to help us ensure the system is working correctly.

Please note: If you confirmed receipt either via email, text message or phone call, the system marked you as having received the notification and should have stopped sending messages via the other methods. 

If you did not receive a notification, check your contact information in Dayforce. If that is correct, then contact the Department of Technology (DoT) Service Desk at 614-645-5758 to let them know so they can help ensure you receive future notifications. If you have not updated your contact information in Dayforce, please do so as soon as possible. View this step-by-step guide on how to make those updates. 

Supervisors, please let staff without easy access to email know about the test. We appreciate your help in ensuring this important communication channel is working so we're prepared for inclement weather or other emergencies.

item.title: Celebrate at the Park, Fall Aquatics Session, Explore Your Creativity, Discover the Espy Adaptive Sports Complex
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Celebrate Your Upcoming Event in the Park

Looking for the perfect spot to host your next celebration? Columbus Recreation and Parks has added open air shelters at Flatwood, Maloney and Mock parks—and they’re now available to reserve. These spaces are great for birthday parties, family reunions, showers and more.

We’d love your input! Tell us which parks you’d like to see open-air shelters added to—fill out a brief survey.

Make a Splash This Fall

Ready to dive in? Fall I aquatics registration opens on Tuesday, Sept. 2, at 12:30 p.m., with classes running Sept. 8-Nov. 2. Choose from swimming lessons or water fitness programs—there’s something for all ages and skill levels

Spots fill quickly - get ready to register!

Falling for New Creative Projects

Registration for session 5 is almost here, and it’s the perfect time to unleash your creativity! 

Registration for classes at the Priscilla R. Tyson Cultural Arts Center opens on Saturday, Aug. 30,  at 8:30 a.m.; classes run Sept. 8-Oct. 31. Explore classes in painting and ceramics to quilting, sewing and mixed media.

Registration for classes at the Fran Ryan Center opens on Tuesday, Sept. 2, at 9 a.m.; classes run Sept. 8-Nov. 1. This session, the center’s sewing studio offers affordable classes and workshops perfect for the holiday season. Learn to quilt, sew, crochet, knit or modify clothing, or explore mixed media art. Whether you’re building skills or starting fresh, the Sewing Studio has something for you!

Discover the Espy Adaptive Sports Complex

The newly renovated Espy Adaptive Sports Complex is designed to make recreation accessible for everyone. Formerly the Franklin Park Adventure Center, the facility supports therapeutic programs. Renamed in honor of Ben and Kathy Espy, the complex continues their legacy of inclusion and opportunity for all.

Join us for the open house to tour the space, meet staff and try hands-on demonstrations such as boccia, wheelchair basketball, wheelchair rugby and adaptive fitness. Stop by 1755 E. Broad St., 43203, on Wednesday, Sept. 3, 4-7 p.m. 

We hope to see you there!

item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

We Want Your Feedback – Help Us Improve CRPD Policies

Dear CRPD Team,

As part of our commitment to continuous improvement, the Legal & Policy team is conducting a quick survey to better understand how staff engage with our department’s policies and procedures—and how we can make them clearer, more useful, and easier to follow.

It takes less than 2 minutes to complete and is completely anonymous. Your honest feedback will help us identify where things are working well and where we can strengthen our support for staff and the communities we serve.

Please complete the survey by Wednesday, May 21.

Take The Survey Now

Your input will directly shape the way we improve processes and prioritize future policy updates—so thank you for being part of the solution.

We appreciate your time and voice!

Best Regards,

Stephen Dyer
Legal & Policy Manager
